signalDesk.scope: Local extension of the existing monograph; public-data demo separate from client evidence.

layout.columns: Three source columns above a full-width brief; two finding columns
layout.intermediateColumns: Source statuses stack within their columns at 1000px
layout.mobile: At 760px, stack findings and ledger fields; retain compact source rail; 18px inset.

signalDesk.sources: Real tool events update querying, completed, outside-coverage or unavailable text; success green denotes retrieval only. Collection times are separate from observation and generation times. Cached completion is labeled recent result.
signalDesk.ledger: Closed by default; citation opens the disclosure. Preview two records per provider; expand to every retrieved record; collapse to preview. Citation filters exact IDs or falls back to sources, focuses heading and scrolls. Clearing filter exposes the complete retrieved set.
signalDesk.coverage: Global: US NWS, worldwide natural events and earthquakes. Panama: 1,000km event radius, outside NWS coverage. Newark: 750km events, point NWS alerts. NASA 30-day catalog capped at 100; USGS 7-day M4.5+; cache up to ten minutes.
signalDesk.brief: Large headline, concise summary, at most two findings with follow-up actions. Native disclosures contain explanations, citations and unknowns. Claims stay within sampled evidence; no absence-of-risk or shipping-impact inference.
signalDesk.accessibility: Pressed scope and citation states, polite live execution strip, busy report, alert/retry errors, focusable ledger heading. Reduced motion disables pulse and smooth citation scroll.

components.name: Document workflow explanation
components.description: Four-stage explanatory ordered list beneath real document evidence, with human review in cobalt. This is prose, not product UI.
components.html:
From one email to an order

Workflow / Implementation and validation
  1. Receive

    Group the email and attachments by customer and shipment type.

  2. Extract and match

    Read the documents and match company, airport, and port codes.

  3. Review and approve

    Flag discrepancies and missing values for operator correction and approval.

    Operator judgment
  4. Check and integrate

    Check existing orders, then connect approved values to KEROL.

narrative.overview:
A neutral technical portfolio makes actual software the visual material. Cool-white ground, ink headings, and cobalt actions hold together work with very different interfaces. Pretendard carries both Korean and English, from the role statement to compact project metadata.

Projects read as exhibits: a product name, subtitle, and context identify the work before its actual media and concrete explanation. Thin rules and open columns establish structure; dark product stages and the contact field provide contrast without introducing a separate identity.
keyCharacteristics: Cool-white surfaces, dark ink, and cobalt interaction states.
One self-hosted bilingual sans serif with a controlled heading hierarchy.
Actual product captures, square frames, and visible contextual information.
Equal project and collaborator contact paths, with keyboard-accessible controls.

rules.name: The Evidence Frame Rule
rules.body: Keep site chrome neutral; color inside actual product captures belongs to the product and does not become a site token.

rules.name: The Reading Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Use readable body text for explanations and compact labels for metadata. Preserve Korean word boundaries and English whitespace; keep heading tracking no tighter than -0.035em.

rules.name: The Media Depth Rule
rules.body: Keep page sections flat; reserve soft shadows for actual media and its stage.

dos: Do identify each project with its name, subtitle, and context before its media and explanation.
Do pair actual product evidence with readable context and a named enlargement action or full-image link where detailed inspection is needed.
Do preserve the complete monitoring interface and its surrounding information panels when presenting the system; let viewers inspect it in fit and original-size modes.
Do distinguish actual interface captures from explanatory workflow diagrams, and keep evidence scope visible in captions and viewer notes.
Do use Pretendard across Korean and English, with explanatory body text at 16px desktop and 15px mobile.
Do retain visible focus, pressed scope states, keyboard-operable citations, and reduced-motion support.
Do keep business inquiries and collaborator contact paths equal in hierarchy and action styling.
donts: Don't restore the rejected serif identity, warm paper palette, or ornamental bookish framing.
Don't replace actual product evidence with invented interface illustrations or decorative typographic mockups.
Don't make small text embedded in screenshots the only source of an important explanation.
Don't turn one product's colors or a compact metadata size into a default for the whole site.
Don't add a rounded card, input, chip, or general-purpose modal family that the build does not implement.
